All I can register is an immense, throbbing pain in my head that has been pounding for the past four‑to‑five hours—since I first regained a sliver of consciousness after days of darkness caused by a sudden seizure.  

The navy nurses tell me it’s been roughly five hours since I opened my eyes, since Tuesday at 5 a.m., when the seizure knocked me out. I was lucky enough that two navy security details were assigned to watch over me—both for my own safety and to alert the base transfer manager should any unforeseen emergency arise from our enemies, given the precarious state of my health and the threats looming from organization sector A.

My experience is different, even after enduring a painful, prolonged blackout.
